questions.question: Which of the following is the formula for elasticity of supply?

options.text: % change in price /% change in quantity supplied
% change in quantity supplied / % change in price
Change in quantity supplied / original quantity supplied

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**% change in quantity supplied / % change in price**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Price Elasticity of Supply (PES)** is an economic measure that quantifies the responsiveness of the **quantity supplied** of a particular good or service to a change in its **market price**.

• The fundamental formula for calculating this coefficient is the **percentage change in quantity supplied** divided by the **percentage change in price**.

• Mathematically, it can be represented as: **Es = (ΔQs / Qs) ÷ (ΔP / P)**, where **ΔQs** represents the change in quantity, **Qs** is the initial quantity, **ΔP** is the change in price, and **P** is the initial price.

• According to the **Law of Supply**, producers typically increase the quantity supplied when prices rise; therefore, the **elasticity of supply** usually results in a **positive value**, reflecting the direct relationship between price and supply.

• The concept was popularized by **Alfred Marshall** and is critical for understanding **market equilibrium** and how producers adjust production levels in response to **market fluctuations**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Degrees of Elasticity of Supply**:

• **Perfectly Inelastic Supply (Es = 0)**: Occurs when the quantity supplied does not change regardless of the price level, often seen in **fixed assets** like **land** or **perishable goods** in the ultra-short run.

• **Inelastic Supply (Es 1)**: The percentage change in quantity supplied exceeds the percentage change in price, common for **manufactured industrial goods** that can be easily scaled.

• **Perfectly Elastic Supply (Es = ∞)**: At a specific price, producers are willing to supply an **infinite quantity**, but if the price falls, the supply drops to zero instantly.

questions.question: Excluding borrowings, the excess of total expenditure over total receipts signifies which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal deficit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is defined as the difference between the **Total Expenditure** (both revenue and capital) and **Total Receipts** (revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts) of the government.
 
• It represents the **total borrowing requirements** of the government from all sources, including the **Reserve Bank of India**, the domestic market, and external sources.
 
• The formula is expressed as: **Fiscal Deficit** = **Total Expenditure** − (**Revenue Receipts** + **Non-Debt Creating Capital Receipts**).
 
• **Non-debt creating capital receipts** include funds generated from the **recovery of loans** and **disinvestment** (sale of shares in public sector undertakings).
 
• A higher **fiscal deficit** indicates that the government is spending beyond its means and must rely on **debt** to finance the gap, which can lead to **inflationary pressures** and increased **interest burdens** in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Deficit**:

 
 
• It occurs when **revenue expenditure** exceeds **revenue receipts**.
 
• It indicates that the government is unable to meet its **regular and recurring expenses**, such as salaries, pensions, and interest payments, from its current income.
 
 
 
• **Primary Deficit**:
 
 
• It is calculated by subtracting **interest payments** on previous borrowings from the current year’s **fiscal deficit**.
 
• Formula: **Primary Deficit** = **Fiscal Deficit** − **Interest Payments**.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Deficit**:
 
 
• This was a traditional term referring to the difference between **total receipts** (including borrowings) and **total expenditure**.
 
• In the current Indian accounting system, the concept of **Budgetary Deficit** has been largely replaced by the **Fiscal Deficit** to provide a clearer picture of government liabilities.
 
 
 
• **Monetized Deficit**:
 
 
• This refers specifically to the part of the **fiscal deficit** that is financed by the **Reserve Bank of India** through the printing of new currency or selling **Treasury Bills**.

questions.question: The difference between the Gross National Product (GNP) and the Net National Product (NNP) is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Depreciation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Gross National Product (GNP)** represents the total market value of all final goods and services produced by the residents of a country, regardless of their location, during a specific financial year.

• **Net National Product (NNP)** is the value obtained by subtracting **Depreciation** from the **Gross National Product**. It provides a more accurate measure of the actual economic growth by accounting for the loss in value of fixed assets.

• **Depreciation**, often referred to as the **Consumption of Fixed Capital (CFC)**, is the monetary value assigned to the wear and tear, obsolescence, or accidental damage of fixed assets like **machinery**, **buildings**, and **equipment** used in production.

• The fundamental accounting identity in national income statistics is expressed as: **NNP = GNP − Depreciation**. This subtraction ensures that the capital consumed in the production process is replaced or accounted for, yielding the 'net' contribution to the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Taxes**:

• In macroeconomics, **Indirect Taxes** (like GST) and **Subsidies** are used to convert **Factor Cost** to **Market Price**.

• **Net Indirect Taxes (NIT)** is the difference between **Indirect Taxes** and **Subsidies**.

• **Interest**:

• This is a **Factor Payment** made to those who provide capital for production. It is a component used in the **Income Method** of calculating national income.

• **Dividend**:

• This represents the part of **Corporate Profit** distributed to shareholders. It is a key element of **Private Income** and **Personal Income**.

• **Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**:

• This is the value that differentiates **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** from **Gross National Product (GNP)**. It is calculated as income earned by domestic residents from abroad minus income earned by foreign residents within the domestic territory.

questions.question: What is the major benefit of the Indian Data Relay Satellite System (IDRSS)?

options.text: Real-time communication with low Earth orbit satellites and astronauts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Real-time communication with low Earth orbit satellites and astronauts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Data Relay Satellite System (IDRSS)** is a planned constellation of communication satellites developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to track and maintain constant contact with Indian satellites.
 
• It is primarily designed to facilitate **real-time, continuous data transfer** between ground stations and satellites operating in **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**, which otherwise have very short windows of visibility to terrestrial antennas.
 
• The system is fundamental to the success of the **Gaganyaan mission**, as it allows for uninterrupted **voice and data communication** with **astronauts** and the **crew module** throughout their orbit around the Earth.
 
• By positioning **IDRSS** satellites in the **Geostationary Orbit (GEO)** at an altitude of nearly **36,000 kilometers**, they can act as a bridge, relaying critical **telemetry**, **tracking**, and **command (TT&C)** data without the coverage gaps inherent in ground-based networks.
 
• The deployment of this network ensures that **mission controllers** at the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** can monitor the health of the spacecraft and receive scientific data in high-definition without delay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deep Space Exploration**

 
 
• Unlike **LEO** relay systems, missions to the **Moon** or **Mars** like **Chandrayaan** and **Mangalyaan** rely on the **Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN)**, which uses massive **32-meter** parabolic antennas for long-distance communication.
 
 
 
• **Solar Energy from Space**
 
 
• This refers to **Space-Based Solar Power (SBSP)**, a conceptual technology that harvests **renewable energy** in orbit to transmit it back to Earth via **microwaves**, which is not the function of **IDRSS**.
 
 
 
• **Satellite Internet Access**
 
 
• Providing **broadband** to **rural areas** is the objective of **High Throughput Satellites (HTS)** such as **GSAT-11** and **GSAT-20**, which utilize multiple **spot beams** to deliver high-speed data directly to consumers.

questions.question: The Chahalgani (Group of Forty) nobles were formed during the reign of:
questions.solution:

• **Iltutmish** (reigned **1211−1236 AD**), the third ruler of the **Mamluk Dynasty**, is credited with the creation of the **Turkan-i-Chahalgani**, also known as the **Corps of Forty**.

• The **Chahalgani** was an elite body of forty loyal **Turkish slave officers** who were handpicked by the Sultan to manage the administration and military affairs of the **Delhi Sultanate**.

• The formation of this group was a strategic move by **Iltutmish** to counter the influence of senior **Ghurid nobles** and to consolidate his power after the death of **Qutb-ud-din Aibak**.

• These nobles held significant positions such as **Iqtadars** (land-grant holders) and played a crucial role in maintaining the stability of the empire against internal rebellions and **Mongol** threats.

• The group functioned as the executive council of the Sultan, although they eventually became so powerful that they started interfering in the **succession** of the throne after **Iltutmish** died.

• **Balban**:

• He was originally a member of the **Chahalgani** but later became the Sultan of Delhi.

• Recognizing that the group posed a threat to the **absolute monarchy**, he systematically eliminated its members to restore the prestige of the crown.

• He is famous for his policy of **Blood and Iron** and the introduction of **Sijda** and **Paibos** (prostration and kissing the Sultan's feet).

questions.question: What kind of architectural feature are the Jain temples known for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Highly intricate marble carvings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jain architecture** is renowned for its superlative use of **white marble**, featuring carvings so delicate and precise they are often compared to **fine lace** or ivory work.
 
• The **Dilwara Temples** on **Mount Abu** in **Rajasthan**, constructed between the **11th and 13th centuries CE**, serve as the most prominent examples of this **intricate marble craftsmanship**.
 
• The **Ranakpur Jain Temple** in the **Pali district** is another architectural marvel, featuring **1,444 uniquely carved marble pillars** where no two pillars share the same design.
 
• Architectural elements such as **ceilings**, **doorways**, and **toranas** (arches) are decorated with complex **floral motifs**, **geometric patterns**, and figures of **Vidyadevis** (goddesses of knowledge).
 
• The use of **Makrana marble** allowed artisans to achieve a level of **translucent detailing** and deep undercutting that is rare in other temple architectures of **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maru-Gurjara Architecture:**

 
 
• This style originated in **Western India** (Gujarat and Rajasthan) and is characterized by its focus on **structural ornamentation** and **sculptural beauty**.
 
• It emphasizes the **Shikhara** (temple spire) and the **Mandapa** (pillared hall) as central aesthetic components.
 
 
 
• **Gothic vaults and arches:**
 
 
• These are defining features of **European Medieval architecture**, utilizing **pointed arches** and **flying buttresses**, which are absent in traditional Jain structures.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other styles:**
 
 
• While **Chola architecture** is known for massive **stone structures** and **bronze icons**, and **Indo-Islamic architecture** features **large domes**, Jain architecture remains distinct through its **micro-level marble ornamentation**.

questions.question: For which architectural element is the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque in Gujarat famous for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lattice windows (jalis)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sidi Saiyyed Mosque**, popularly known as **Sidi Saiyyed ni Jali**, was built in **1572-73 AD** in **Ahmedabad**, **Gujarat**.
 
• It was constructed by **Sidi Saiyyed**, an Abyssinian nobleman in the service of **Bilal Jhajhar Khan**, during the reign of the last Sultan of the **Gujarat Sultanate**, **Muzaffar Shah III**.
 
• The structure is world-famous for its ten beautifully carved semi-circular **lattice windows** (**jalis**) that adorn the side and rear arches of the mosque.
 
• The most iconic of these is the **Tree of Life** jali, which features a central tree with intertwining branches and foliage, showcasing unparalleled **Indo-Saracenic** craftsmanship.
 
• The delicate stone carving is so fine that it resembles **filigree** work, representing the height of the **Gujarat School of Architecture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Significance**:

 
 
• The **Tree of Life** design is the inspiration behind the logo of the **Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA)**.
 
• Unlike many other mosques of that era, the **Sidi Saiyyed Mosque** does not have a traditional courtyard, as it was built as part of the **citadel wall**.
 
• The central arch of the mosque is surprisingly devoid of a jali, likely due to the **Mughal invasion** of Gujarat in **1573** by **Emperor Akbar**, which halted the completion of the work.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Heritage**:
 
 
• The mosque is considered one of the finest examples of **Islamic art** in India, blending local **Hindu** and **Jain** motifs with Islamic architectural geometry.
 
• The city of **Ahmedabad**, where the mosque is located, was declared India's first **UNESCO World Heritage City** in **2017**.

questions.question: Where was the Bhilai Steel Plant set up in 1959?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP)** is located in **Bhilai**, situated in the **Durg district** of the modern-day state of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It was established in **1955** following a bilateral agreement between the Government of **India** and the **USSR (Soviet Union)**.
 
• The plant became operational in **1959** when the first blast furnace was commissioned, marking a significant milestone in India's **industrialization** journey during the **Second Five-Year Plan**.
 
• The location was strategically selected due to its proximity to the **Dalli-Rajhara iron ore mines**, which are approximately 100 km away, and the **Korba coal fields**.
 
• The **Bhilai Steel Plant** is managed by the **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)** and is renowned for being the primary producer of high-quality **steel rails** for the **Indian Railways**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956−1961)**:

 
 
• Based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, this plan prioritized the development of heavy industries and capital goods.
 
• Three major integrated steel plants were set up: **Bhilai** (Soviet collaboration), **Rourkela** (German collaboration), and **Durgapur** (British collaboration).
 
 
 
• **Odisha**:
 
 
• This state is home to the **Rourkela Steel Plant**, which was the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India, established with assistance from **Krupp and Demag** of **Germany**.
 
 
 
• **Jamshedpur**:

What was the most objectionable aspect of these Acts?

options.text: They imposed heavy taxes on Indian businesses and traders.

__
 
• The **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, popularly known as the **Rowlatt Act**, was passed by the **Imperial Legislative Council** in **Delhi** on **March 18, 1919**.
 
• The most contentious provision of this legislation was the authorization of the **British colonial government** to arrest and imprison individuals suspected of **sedition** or **revolutionary activities** for up to **two years** without a jury trial or any judicial proceedings.
 
• This act effectively suspended the principle of **Habeas Corpus**, a legal recourse that protects individuals against arbitrary state detention, thereby granting the executive branch unchecked power over personal liberty.
 
• Indian leaders and nationalists condemned the law as the **Black Act**, describing it with the slogan **No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal**, highlighting the denial of the right to legal counsel, the right to present evidence, and the right to appeal.
 
• The act was intended to suppress the growing **nationalist upsurge** and political unrest that followed **World War I** by providing extraordinary powers to the police and administration.

• The severe government crackdown on these protests directly culminated in the tragic **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** on **April 13, 1919**, in **Amritsar**.

• **Compulsory registration** of citizens was a feature of the **Asiatic Registration Act** in the **Transvaal** (South Africa), which Gandhi had previously fought against in **1906**.
 
• The **Rowlatt Act** was specifically designed for **political suppression** rather than **economic taxation** or the empowerment of **local self-governing bodies**.

questions.question:
The "Indian Forest Act" of 1878 categorized forests into reserved and protected areas.

What was a key difference in the treatment and rights of local communities between these two categories?

options.text: Both categories granted complete autonomy to local communities in forest management.

__
 
• The **Indian Forest Act of 1878** was a colonial legislative measure designed to consolidate **British** control over **India's forest resources**, classifying them into **Reserved**, **Protected**, and **Village forests**.
 
• **Reserved Forests** were the most restricted category; the government claimed full ownership of these areas, which contained the most valuable timber like **Teak** and **Sal**. In these zones, all **customary rights** of local communities, including **grazing**, **collection of minor forest produce**, and **entry**, were **legally extinguished** unless specific permission was granted.
 
• In contrast, **Protected Forests** allowed for some **limited rights**. While the government still owned the land, local communities could often access these areas for **firewood** or **grazing**, provided they did not damage the species protected for commercial use. The legal logic was that everything was **permitted unless specifically prohibited**.
 
• This classification system effectively turned forest dwellers into **encroachers** on their own ancestral lands, prioritizing the **commercial extraction** of timber for **railway sleepers** and **shipbuilding** over the subsistence needs of **indigenous populations**.

• He introduced **Scientific Forestry**, which replaced natural biodiversity with **plantations** of specific industrial species to ensure a steady supply of timber.
 
 
 
• **Village Forests**:
 
 
• The third category established by the **1878 Act**, where portions of **reserved forests** could be assigned to village communities for their direct use, though this provision was rarely utilized by the administration.
 
 
 
• **Social Consequences**:
 
 
• The restrictions led to widespread **hardship** and **displacement** for **Adivasi** communities, triggering major historical uprisings like the **Bastar Rebellion** of **1910** and movements led by **Birsa Munda**.

• According to the **Puranic** texts and the **Harshacharita** written by **Banabhatta**, Devabhuti was described as a weak and dissolute ruler who was overly fond of the company of women, leading to his downfall.
 
• His reign came to a violent end in **73 BCE** when he was assassinated by his own minister, **Vasudeva Kanva**. This event marked the total collapse of the **Sunga Empire** and the rise of the **Kanva Dynasty** in **Magadha**.
 
• The **Sunga Dynasty** overall lasted for about **112 years**, serving as a critical period for the revival of **Brahmanical traditions** and the patronage of art and architecture, notably the expansion of the **Sanchi Stupa** and the **Bharhut Stupa**.

• He was the **founder** of the Sunga Dynasty and the **Senapati** (Commander-in-Chief) of the last Mauryan King, **Brihadratha**.
 
• He ascended the throne in **185 BCE** and is famous for performing two **Ashvamedha Yagyas** (horse sacrifices) to assert his imperial authority.

questions.question: Which among the following statements is TRUE about the Rig Vedic Society?

options.text: The Rig Vedic society was matrilineal.
The head of the family was known as Vishaypati.
Apala, Visvavara, Ghosa, and Lopamudra were prominent women poets of the Rig Vedic period.
Child marriage and the practice of Sati were prevalent.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apala, Visvavara, Ghosa, and Lopamudra were prominent women poets of the Rig Vedic period.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rig Vedic society** was primarily **patriarchal** (patrilineal) in nature, where the eldest male member or father held authority over the family unit. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• The basic unit of society was the **Kula** (family). The head of the family was known as the **Kulapa** or **Grihapati**, whereas the **Vishaypati** was the head of a **Vish** (a group of villages). Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• Women in the **Early Vedic period** enjoyed a high status and were provided opportunities for spiritual and intellectual development. Renowned female scholars like **Apala**, **Visvavara**, **Ghosa**, and **Lopamudra** attained the status of **Rishis** and composed several hymns in the **Rig Veda**. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• Social evils like **child marriage** and the custom of **Sati** were generally non-existent during this era. Girls were married only after attaining maturity, and they often had a say in choosing their life partners. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Hierarchy**:

 
 
• **Kula**: The smallest unit, headed by the **Kulapa**.
 
• **Grama**: A collection of families, headed by the **Gramani**.
 
• **Vish**: A tribal division composed of several villages, led by the **Vishaypati**.
 
• **Jana**: The highest political or tribal unit, ruled by the **Rajan** (King).
 
 
 
• **Position of Women**:
 
 
• Women were allowed to attend assemblies like the **Sabha** and **Vidatha**.
 
• The practice of **Niyoga** (widow remarriage) was permitted, especially if the woman was childless.
 
• They were entitled to undergo the **Upanayana** ceremony and receive an education.
 
 
 
• **Social Practices**:
 
 
• The society was divided into four **Varnas** (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras), but the system was flexible and based on occupation rather than birth during the **Early Vedic** stage.
 
• Monogamy was the standard, although **polygyny** was sometimes practiced by the nobility and **Rishis**.

questions.question: In the alluvial plains of the Ganga, which of the following physical features will NOT be found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rapids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **alluvial plains** of the **Ganga** are characterized by a very **gentle gradient** and deep deposits of **alluvium**, where the river performs lateral erosion and deposition rather than vertical cutting.
 
• **Rapids** are hydrological features where the river bed has a relatively **steep gradient**, causing an increase in water velocity and **turbulence**. These are typically found in the **Upper Course** (mountainous stage) of a river.
 
• In the **Himalayan reach** of the Ganga, rapids and **gorges** are common; however, once the river enters the plains at **Haridwar**, the decrease in slope makes the formation of rapids physically impossible.
 
• The **Ganga Plain** is part of the **Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra** plain, which is a **foredeep** basin filled with sediments. In such flat terrains, the river energy is insufficient to maintain the turbulence required for rapids.
 
• Features like **oxbow lakes**, **meanders**, and **braided channels** are classic landforms of the **mature and old stages** of a river, which define the geomorphology of the **Ganga basin**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxbow Lakes**:

 
 
• These are U-shaped bodies of water formed when a wide **meander** is cut off from the main river channel.
 
• In the **Middle Ganga Plain**, these are frequently seen in states like **Bihar** and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Meanders**:
 
 
• Sinuous curves or loops in the course of a river caused by **lateral erosion** on the outer bank and **deposition** on the inner bank.
 
• The **Ganga** exhibits high **sinuosity** in its middle reach due to the soft alluvial soil and low slope.
 
 
 
• **Braided Channels**:
 
 
• A network of river channels separated by small, often temporary, islands called **braid bars** or eyots.
 
• This occurs when the river carries a high **sediment load**, common in the **lower reaches** and the **deltaic region** of the Ganga and Brahmaputra.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Angami Sekrenyi festival?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Sekrenyi** festival is the premier annual event of the **Angami Naga** tribe of **Nagaland**, which serves as a major cultural landmark for the community.
 
• The primary objective of the festival is **Phousanyi**, a term that signifies **purification**. It is observed to **cleanse the body and soul** of all past transgressions and misfortunes, seeking spiritual renewal.
 
• The celebration lasts for **ten days** and begins on the 25th day of the month of **Kezei** (which usually falls in February), marking the start of the **Angami lunar year**.
 
• A central theme of the festival is to bring **unity** and **sanctification** to the community, ensuring that the villagers enter the new agricultural cycle with a pure spirit and a healthy body.

• **Ritualistic Highlights**:

questions.question:
Which Hindustani classical gharana, founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan, is known for its melodic complexity and features exponents like

Kesarbai Kerkar and Kishori Amonkar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana** was established by **Ustad Alladiya Khan** (1855−1946) in the late **19th century**. He was originally from **Atrauli** and later served in the courts of **Jaipur** and **Kolhapur**, merging these diverse musical influences.
 
• This gharana is globally recognized for its extreme **melodic complexity** and a technical singing style known as **Gund-Gunkari**, which involves intricate ornamentation and weaving of notes.
 
• A defining feature of this school is the use of **Vakra Taans** (oblique or convoluted melodic phrases). These patterns are non-linear and require immense breath control and **Raaga** knowledge to execute without losing the rhythmic cycle.
 
• The repertoire predominantly features **Aprachalit Raagas** (rare raagas) and **Jod Raagas** (compound raagas) such as **Lalita-Gauri**, **Jaitashree**, and **Sampoorna-Malkouns**, rather than common scales.
 
• Exponents like **Kesarbai Kerkar**, who was a **Padma Bhushan** recipient, and **Kishori Amonkar**, known for her innovative **Ras-Siddhant** approach, are the most celebrated figures of this tradition.
 
• The singing is characterized by a **steady medium tempo** (Madhya Laya), avoiding the very slow **Vilambit** used by other schools, ensuring a tight integration between **Swar** (note) and **Laya** (rhythm).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gwalior Gharana**

 
 
• Regarded as the **mother of all gharanas**, it was founded by **Ustad Hassu Khan** and **Haddu Khan**.
 
• Focuses on **lucidity**, simple **straight taans**, and the structural purity of the **Bandish**.
 
 
 
• **Agra Gharana**
 
 
• Founded by **Haji Sujan Khan** and later redefined by **Ustad Faiyaz Khan**, also known as **Aftab-e-Mausiqi**.
 
• Known for its **powerful resonance**, use of **Nom-Tom Alap**, and strong rhythmic play (**Layakari**).
 
 
 
• **Kirana Gharana**
 
 
• Established by **Ustad Abdul Karim Khan** and **Ustad Abdul Wahid Khan**, focusing heavily on **perfect intonation** (Swar).
 
• Famous for the **Barhat** technique, where the **Raaga** is expanded note-by-note with great emotional depth.

questions.question: Which of the following physiographic features acts as the principal water divide in Peninsular India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Ghats**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Western Ghats**, also known as the **Sahyadri**, constitute a continuous mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula for nearly **1,600 kilometers**.

• This physiographic feature acts as the **principal water divide** of **Peninsular India** because it separates the drainage basins of the rivers flowing into the **Arabian Sea** from those flowing into the **Bay of Bengal**.

• Most major perennial rivers of the peninsula, such as the **Godavari**, **Krishna**, and **Kaveri**, originate on the eastern slopes of these ghats and flow eastward across the **Deccan Plateau** due to its gentle tilt.

• Conversely, the western slopes are steep, causing rainfall from the **Southwest Monsoon** to feed short, swift, and non-perennial streams that drain directly into the **Arabian Sea**.

• The range remains largely unbroken, with only a few gaps like the **Palakkad Gap**, ensuring its role as a formidable barrier that directs the flow of water across the subcontinent.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Vindhya Range**:

• This range is located in **Central India** and separates the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** from the **Deccan Plateau**.

• It acts as a primary divide between the **Ganga river system** and the southward-flowing river systems like the **Narmada**.

• **Aravalli Hills**:

• These are among the oldest **fold mountains** in the world, stretching from **Gujarat** through **Rajasthan** to **Delhi**.

• They function as a water divide between the **Indus basin** (Luni and Sakhi rivers) and the **Ganga basin** (Banas and Chambal rivers).

• **Eastern Ghats**:

• This is a **discontinuous** and eroded mountain range running along India’s eastern coast from **Odisha** to **Tamil Nadu**.

• They do not serve as a principal water divide because major rivers originating in the west cut through them to reach the **Bay of Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorophyll a** is the primary **photosynthetic pigment** found in the **chloroplasts** of all **oxygen-evolving photosynthetic organisms**, such as **vascular plants**, **algae**, and **cyanobacteria**.
 
• It serves as the **reaction center** in both **Photosystem I (P700)** and **Photosystem II (P680)**, where it converts **solar energy** into **chemical energy**.
 
• This pigment exhibits maximum absorption in the **blue-violet** (approximately **430 nm**) and **red** (approximately **660 nm**) regions of the **visible light spectrum**.
 
• While it absorbs red and blue light, it reflects **green light**, which is why most plant leaves appear green to the human eye.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorophyll b**:

 
 
• Functioning as an **accessory pigment**, it assists **Chlorophyll a** by broadening the range of light wavelengths that can be used for **photosynthesis**.
 
• It primarily absorbs **blue** and **orange light** and is found mainly in **land plants** and **green algae**.
 
 
 
• **Carotenoids**:
 
 
• These are **lipid-soluble** pigments that produce **yellow, orange, and red** colors in plants.
 
• They perform **photoprotection** by dissipating excess **light energy** that could damage **chlorophyll** molecules through **photo-oxidation**.
 
 
 
• **Anthocyanins**:
 
 
• These are **water-soluble** pigments located in the **cell vacuole** that provide **red, purple, or blue** coloration to **flowers** and **fruits**.
 
• Unlike chlorophyll, they do not participate in the **light-dependent reactions** of photosynthesis but help in **pollinator attraction** and **stress resistance**.

questions.question:
Consider the following:

(1) DPIIT handles industrial promotion.

(2) It implements Gati Shakti.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**, operating under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, is responsible for the formulation and implementation of promotional measures for the growth of the industrial sector in India. It oversees industrial policy and coordinates the development of various sectors. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **PM Gati Shakti** National Master Plan is a digital platform designed to bring 16 Ministries, including Railways and Roadways, together for integrated planning and coordinated implementation of infrastructure connectivity projects. The **DPIIT** serves as the nodal department for monitoring and implementing this master plan. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DPIIT Functions**:

 
 
• Formerly known as the **Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP)**, it was renamed in **January 2019** to incorporate internal trade and trader welfare.
 
• The department is the nodal body for matters related to **Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs)**, including patents, designs, and trademarks.
 
• It manages the **Startup India** initiative and monitors **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** inflows into the country.
 
 
 
• **PM Gati Shakti**:
 
 
• Launched in **October 2021** with a budget outlay of approximately **100 lakh crore**.
 
• It utilizes **GIS-based** spatial planning tools to provide real-time visibility for infrastructure projects across the country.
 
• The initiative focuses on **six pillars**: Comprehensiveness, Prioritization, Optimization, Synchronization, Analytical, and Dynamic.

questions.question: What is a key benefit provided under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Free delivery and C-section services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)** was launched by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)** on **1st June 2011** to provide completely free and cashless services to pregnant women and sick newborns.
 
• The scheme guarantees **free and cashless delivery**, which includes both **normal vaginal deliveries** and surgical **Caesarean sections (C-sections)** at all public health institutions.
 
• It aims to eliminate **out-of-pocket expenses (OOPE)** incurred by pregnant women and their families, thereby encouraging **institutional deliveries** to reduce the **Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)** and **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)**.
 
• Under JSSK, pregnant women are entitled to **free drugs and consumables**, **free diagnostics** (including blood and urine tests and ultrasounds), and **free blood transfusion** services if required.
 
• The initiative also provides a **free diet** for the duration of the hospital stay (up to **3 days** for normal delivery and up to **7 days** for a C-section).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transport Services**:

 
 
• Contrary to the concept of 'paid transport', JSSK provides **free transport** from home to the health facility and between facilities in case of **referral**.
 
• It also includes a **free drop-back** from the facility to the patient's home after a mandatory stay of **48 hours** post-delivery.
 
 
 
• **Sick Infant Coverage**:
 
 
• The scheme covers **sick infants** up to **one year** of age (expanded from the initial 30 days) for all treatment-related costs in public hospitals.
 
• This includes **free medicines**, **diagnostics**, and **transportation** to ensure timely medical intervention for pediatric emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Exemption from User Charges**:
 
 
• JSSK mandates that no **user charges** are to be levied for any services provided to the mother or the infant, including registration fees or bed charges.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about E. Sreedharan is factually correct?

options.text: He led the development of the Mumbai-Pune Expressway.
He was popularly known as the 'Metro Man of India'.
He drafted the Indian Road Safety Code.
He was responsible for launching the Swachh Bharat Mission.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He was popularly known as the 'Metro Man of India'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• E. Sreedharan did not lead the development of the **Mumbai-Pune Expressway**, as that project was a landmark achievement of the **Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• He is famously known as the **'Metro Man of India'** for his transformative leadership in the **Delhi Metro** project and for completing the **Konkan Railway** project against extreme geographical odds. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Drafting the **Indian Road Safety Code** was not among his primary professional contributions, as his expertise focused on civil engineering and **railway infrastructure**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Swachh Bharat Mission** is a nationwide cleanliness campaign launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **2nd October 2014**, not by E. Sreedharan. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **E. Sreedharan**:

 
 
• He is a retired **Indian Engineering Service (IES)** officer who served as the first Managing Director of the **Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC)**.
 
• He is credited with the restoration of the **Pamban Bridge** in just 46 days after it was damaged by a cyclone in **1964**.
 
• In recognition of his service, the Government of India awarded him the **Padma Shri** in **2001** and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2008**.
 
• He was also conferred with the **Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur** by the French government in **2005** for his work on the Delhi Metro.
 
• His tenure at **Konkan Railway** is celebrated for implementing a 760-km track through 2,000 bridges and 91 tunnels in record time.
